title: _safePay revert in stake()/unstake() blocks principal adjustments during transient shortfall; emergencyWithdraw is the only escape and forfeits all pending
description: Story-002 makes `_safePay` revert if `rewardToken.balanceOf(this) < amount`, correctly closing the prior silent-forfeiture hole in `claim()`. The same `_safePay` is called inside `stake()` and `unstake()` as part of the auto-claim when `user.amount > 0`. Consequence: if pending exceeds the on-contract balance (dispatcher lagging, hook unset/broken, another user just drained the balance in the same block), a user who merely wants to stake MORE or unstake SOME principal CANNOT, because the auto-claim reverts the entire tx. The only fallback is `emergencyWithdraw`, which is all-or-nothing (full exit of principal AND full forfeiture of pending). For a transient shortfall, waiting is fine; for a persistent shortfall, users are trapped between 'cannot adjust' and 'emergency-withdraw forfeits everything'.
impact: Principal adjustments blocked during shortfall windows even when the user would accept a partial payout. Emergency-withdraw is disproportionate when shortfall is small relative to pending. UX regression vs. pre-fix: previously users silently forfeited part of the reward; now they forfeit the whole thing if they need to move.
proof:
1. User has `user.amount = 100`, `pending = 50 phUSD`.
2. Dispatcher hook temporarily unavailable; contract balance drops to 30 phUSD (e.g. another user just claimed).
3. User calls `stake(10)`. `_syncBudget` runs (no hook inflow); `pending = 50`; `_safePay(50)` reverts because `30 < 50`. Entire tx reverts.
4. `unstake(50)` — same revert path.
5. `emergencyWithdraw` returns 100 NFT units but forfeits 50 phUSD pending. User has no proportional option.
suggested-fix: Decouple principal-adjustment from reward-payout: in `stake`/`unstake`, when `_safePay` would revert, ROLL OVER the unpaid portion (`user.rewardDebt = entitlement - unpaid`) so it stays claimable next time, and proceed with the principal change. This preserves the CS-01 no-silent-forfeiture fix while unblocking principal adjustments. Alternative: expose `stakeNoClaim` / `unstakeNoClaim` paths, or a `skipClaim` flag.
consolidation-note: No overlap in ES findings. Standalone.
sanitizer-note: No known-issue match. Concrete UX/locking regression from the story-002 revert change. Keep.
